newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA TAKES FIFTH SLALOM WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA TAKES FIFTH SLALOM WIN.

text.p: Austria's Thomas Sykora continued his domination of the men's World Cup slalom on Sunday as he recorded his fifth win in six races.
Sykora, who led by 0.26 seconds over team mate Thomas Stangassinger after the first run, produced only the sixth best time on his second trip down the deteriorating Lauberhorn course.
But it was still more than enough and the 28-year-old Austrian collected his seventh career win with a two-run combined time of one minute 34.03 seconds.
For Stangassinger it was the third time this season he had settled for second place behind his team mate, finishing with 1:34.36.
Sebastien Amiez of France was third in 1:34.68 ahead of Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt with 1:35.01.

Sykora has dominated the discipline this season the way Italy's Alberto Tomba once did. The only blemish on the lanky Austrian's otherwise perfect record this season was a second place in Breckenridge.
Tomba, twice a winner in Wengen, did not race.
The slalom and giant slalom world champion remained at home recovering for the influenza that forced him out of the second leg of last Sunday's giant slalom in Chamonix, France.
The victory strengthened Sykora's position at the top of the World Cup slalom standings, with 580 points.
Stangassinger is second on 360 with three slaloms left this season.
